NasiruddinMuhammad Humayun
Babur was succeeded by his son Nasiruddin Muhammad Humayun 1530 AD-1556 AD as
a Mughal ruler of India. Humayun ruled twice from 1530 AD to 1540 AD and again from
1555AD to 1556 AD. Some historians view Humayun as a weak ruler because during his
time, some Indian rulers seized the opportunity and dethroned Humayun for more than a
decade. Sher Shah Suri was one of those challengers to Humayun's rule.
Challenges to Humayun's Rule
TheAfghan Interruption
Sher Shah Suri of Pashtun sub tribe rose against Humayun in 1539AD and 1540AD.Sher
Shah Suri defeated Humayun both thetimes in thebattle andfoundedthe Suri Empire in
the northern parts of india. Humayun not only lost the control of the Empire, but he had
also lost his throne.Consequently, in1540 AD,Humayun hadtogo intoforced exile and
SherShah SurioccupiedthethroneofDelhi.
